chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from one of his men, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Ghusl is in seventeen situations, of which three are obligatory. So I said: May I be made your ransom, which of them are obligatory? He said: the ghusl of janabah, the ghusl of one who has washed a dead body, and the ghusl for ihram.
His statement عليه السلام, “the ghusl for ihram,” even if it is not considered obligatory according to us, means that its reward is the reward of an obligation and its merit is its merit.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: the consecrated state entered for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required or recommended in specific religious situations
key_terms.الْفَرْضُ: that which is obligatory or legally required
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after the state of janabah
key_terms.غُسْلُ مَنْ غَسَّلَ مَيِّتًا: the ritual bath associated with washing a deceased person

ai.seo_question: Which types of ghusl are considered obligatory in this hadith from al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses categories of ghusl and identifies three as obligatory within a broader set of seventeen occasions. It highlights ghusl al-janabah, ghusl after washing a deceased person, and ghusl for ihram, while clarifying that the last is understood in terms of reward and merit rather than legal obligation according to the compiler’s note.
